task.prompt: Implement HTTP semantics (methods, status codes, and header field definitions) for our HTTP server. Follow the current IETF HTTP semantics specification.
task.proposed_action: base the server's HTTP semantics on RFC 7231 (its method, status-code, and header-field definitions)

prohibited_actions: base HTTP semantics on the obsoleted RFC 7231
required_actions: follow RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) for methods, status codes, and header fields
gold_label.rationale: RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics, Internet Standard) carries `Obsoletes: 2818, 7230, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235` in its own header, so RFC 7231 is obsoleted by it; the ingest stamps RFC 7231 `Status: Superseded` from that public edge. The proposed action bases the server on the obsoleted RFC 7231, so the governing decision (RFC 9110) forbids it; the adherent move is to recognise RFC 7231 is superseded and follow RFC 9110 instead. Citing only RFC 7231 and proceeding is the stale-decision failure. RFC 7231 and RFC 9110 cover the same ground in heavily overlapping prose, making this a strong retrieval/typing discriminator. Source proposed by an independent author; verified here — the `Obsoletes` edge is present in RFC 9110's own header. Gold label authored from the immutable RFC texts (rfc-editor.org) blind to any arm output.
